[b]Julius' return[/b]
[i]My car took the same route back to Versia, speeding along the uninhabited roads back into our home. A friendly Versian armored escort met us on our way and escorted us to Caprium. There, I was safe. Upon my return to Caprium, I was halted by soldiers of the Ordo Custodum, Versia's religious military arm.

The gates of Caprium were opened, and soldiers of the 6th Stormtrooper Legion were lined up neatly, saluting me as I passed. I returned their salute and made my way to the Imperial Palace. My head hurt from the adrenaline rush, and the fear that I might lose my life only grew as I announce myself before the Rex and his Imperial Court.

(Rex Honorious XIV pov)

Before me were piles upon piles of fresh cut meats, steaks, anything a true Conqueror such as myself could want. I dug in, then stopped as a sudden announcement was brought before me. I watched my personal mini wooden table carrying my food be replaced with an empty floor. A Centurion loudly spoke up.

"My glorious Rex, may you live forever! Announcing Dux Julius Valerian Cassiodorus Vers Allusia, returning from his diplomatic mission in Thyven!" This had better be good if he's returned so quickly. He ran up to me, covered in sweat. He looked defeated, his eyes once again avoiding mine.

"By Jupiter, what's happened to you, Julius? How fared the mission?" He gave me a wild-eyed look, and rose. The Court, abuzz with chatter from the Higher Nobility, fell silent as all eyes were fixed on him.

"The talks... were uncompleted." He was shaking, seeming to take my threat before a little too seriously. Julius knelt down again in reverence. "I was unable to finish my negotiations with Lady Drs of Thyven. Terrorists assaulted the country using hijacked planes, but I couldn't hear much else. I was guided out to my vehicle for my own protection, and we promtly left. Forgive me, my King. I have failed." His eyes were scared, rightfully so. Julius was a talker, not a warrior such as myself. He preferred quiet talks, lavish and exotic foods, particularly sweets, and hated having to deal with war. It came to me as no surprise that he would flee here rather than take cover in a shelter there.

"Very well, Julius." I thought for a moment, feeling great anger and pity. "I'm sorry I pushed you so hard earlier. It was wrong of me to threaten you. I sincerely apologize." I put a hand on his shoulder while he was kneeling in submission. "Your life and family will be spared, with compensation. Can you tell me who attacked you while you were on mission?" 

"I couldn't say, my Rex. Although I've only heard stories and rumors, I do know of a [nation=noflag]Sal-Baliz[/nation], and I think they may have a part to play in this. I hear they have a notorious reputation." I thought for a bit. "Thank you, Julius. You may go and rest, my cousin." I told him. "May the Gods bless you and walk with you." He returned my gaze with tears streaming down his face. Julius stood, saluted, and marched out, presumably back to his city of Iuvavum.

I looked to my Adjutant, who was jotting down notes. She eyed me cautiously.

"My dear Adjutant, summon the Consilium Versiae to Mineros. Lock down all the exits, and make sure our anti-air defenses are still properly maintained. Those bastards who nearly killed my cousin will pay a terrible price for their transgressions." I told her sternly. "Have my Legions gather in Mineros as well, for a speech. I must tell the world what transpired today and tell them that terrorism on this island will not be tolerated." She gave me a nod, bowed, and left. The rest of the Court looked at me expectantly. One glare from me resumed the chatter of the court.
[/i]

[quote=sal-baliz;58964058][b]Hijack[/b]
Early in the morning of 30th March, a group of Sal-Baliz operatives in Thýven made their way to the airport. Disguised as tourists, they split up into three small teams, each team carrying tickets to a different plane. These tickets had been acquired from the Armed Republic of Sikirsk during its final days in power. The teams swiftly made their way through airport security.

You may be wondering how a group of hijackers managed to get past the vigilant security of Thýven. Well, there was no reason for them to be stopped. No guns, no drugs, no knives. They were armed with nothing but their fists; however, this was all they needed. Ever since childhood, these men had been training to hijack flights. They had spent hours learning to master hand-to-hand combat in order to take control of the plane as easily as possible.

At 7:30 a.m., the first plane took off, heading west, but was soon hijacked and taken northeast towards Hydronia instead. The orders of these hijackers were to crash into the Kazaruk base, where five prisoners were being held. The plan was to kill the prisoners before they could reveal any information. The second plane took off at 8:00 a.m. and headed towards Etherniasti, with the intent to crash into a skyscraper in Port Thriump. The final plane took off at 9:15 a.m., initially heading south but was quickly turned back around and headed straight for Tharkønn.The Sal-Baliz claimed that the reason the ARoS collapsed was the invasion by Thýven, so this attack was considered punishment for the brief war.

Panic spread across these nations as word got out that three planes had been hijacked. The Sal-Baliz wanted to make a big strike, and here it was.

[nation]The Crystalline Empire[/nation]
[nation]United Hydronia[/nation]

As soon as Hydronian flight control was made aware of the situation, all flights were halted. In-flight planes were ordered to land in the nearest safe country. Panic swept through airports as travelers were informed of the unfolding crisis. The government was immediately notified of the hijacking, prompting the president to issue an emergency order to dispatch fighter jets to intercept the rogue plane. 

The green squadron quickly took to the air and headed towards the aircraft. The hijackers were intercepted over the Shamat Sea, where multiple stark warnings were issued. However, the plane remained unresponsive. As they neared Kazaruk base, the squadron was compelled to take urgent action. The plane began a rapid descent towards the base, and as soon as the military was alerted about the hijackings, evacuation procedures were initiated. Most personnel managed to escape, but the Sal-Baliz prisoners refused to budge, leading to a tense standoff.

A violent confrontation broke out between the prisoners, armed with anything they could find, and the prison guards. The guards, focused on subduing the prisoners without causing fatalities, resorted to shooting at their legs to immobilize them. Amid the chaos, three prisoners were successfully evacuated along with the majority of the base staff. However, two prisoners and a handful of guards remained behind.

As the green squadron continued their operation, they began firing on the plane, managing to divert it slightly off course. Despite their efforts, the aircraft still managed to land in the northern section of the base, resulting in the tragic deaths of the remaining prisoners and guards. In the aftermath, the government of Hydronia vowed to hold the Sal-Baliz accountable for their actions. Bombings would increase significantly and more units are set to be dispatched into the desert of west shamat.

	When the spies had finally reached their destination, due to the high number of civilians, and the low number of guards, they could only kill about 20 people. In the middle of a three day search, one of the commanding officers heard that someone knew where they were, but was hiding it. A few hours later, sections of the city were called into big buildings. The people who didn't go were to be found and put in prison for a long time. If someone was hiding the truth, they would get it out of him. It wasn't simple questions, but instead it was punishment for wrong answers. You often heard the sounds of someone breaking a finger, or a whip crack from a guard.
